title: Seasonal Hydropower Forecast Framework Using a Combination of Deep Learning and Physics‐Based Methods
content:
Abstract

Seasonal hydropower forecasts can inform power-system resource adequacy, but uncertainty propagates through climate, hydrologic, routing, water-management, and generation components. We develop a regional planning prototype linking North American Multi-Model Ensemble seasonal forecasts, Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) downscaling, an uncertainty-aware long short-term memory runoff model based on Uncountable Mixtures of Asymmetric Laplacians (UMAL-LSTM), MOSART-WM routing and water management, and plant-level autoregressive generation estimates. During 2011–2020, FNO reduced monthly spatially averaged mean absolute error relative to the best non-FNO baseline by 13.0% for precipitation, 16.3% for temperature, and 6.2% for wind speed, although residual biases and complex-terrain errors remained. Runoff evaluation showed broad skill relative to the Global Reach-level Flood Reanalysis reanalysis target; independent streamflow and controlled-forcing checks indicated substantial spatial heterogeneity and contributions from both meteorological downscaling and hydrologic-model limitations. Regional hydropower-generation CRPS Skill Score (CRPSS) was approximately 0.25–0.33 at a 1-month lead. Skill declined with lead and varied by region and season; by month four, several snow- and melt-season regional CRPSS values approached or fell below zero. The framework provides probabilistic hydropower indicators for regional resource-adequacy planning, but it is not a plant-operations model because it does not explicitly represent plant-specific submonthly constraints, flood-control optimization, turbine release versus spill, dynamic hydraulic head, market dispatch, or changing operating priorities.
